metadata.situation: I hate my job but I am scared to quit and seek a new career.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello, what would you like to talk about?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am having a lot of anxiety about quitting my current job. It is too stressful but pays well

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: What makes your job stressful for you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have to deal with many people in hard financial situations and it is upsetting

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you help your clients to make it to a better financial situation?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I do, but often they are not going to get back to what they want. Many people are going to lose their home when safeguards are lifted

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: But you offer them a better future than what they have currently. It may not be what they wanted, but it helps them in the long run.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true but sometimes I feel like I should put my feelings and health first

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I can understand that.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is there another job that would pay you close to what you currently make?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Probably not. I was with the same company for a long time and I consistently get a bonus every year

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is it possible to reframe how you look at your clients' dire financial situations?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I could try. It mostly gets to me at the end of the day

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Some people can't do what you do because they don't have the heart to give someone else bad news. The reality is though, someone needs to fill that role and you do help people

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is also true. Sometimes I wonder if it really is for me though

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I've had to deal with collections before when I was in  bad financial condition. The person on the other line was really helpful though. She was understanding,

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It may not be for you. I think you should think about the pros and cons of keeping your position. It might make things clearer for you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true. Maybe I just need to sit down and really think about it

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I wouldn't stay if it really impacts your mental health in a negative way. Still, you may need to zoom out and see the bigger picture: that you provide a needed service and you do it compassionately

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It really is a big decision

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for the different perspective

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: No doubt, but you know in your heart what is right for you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true. Thanks again

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Bye

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It's no problem. I hope you can make a decision about this situation and then be at peace with it

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok, take care

metadata.situation: I have been out of work for five weeks in quarantine due to testing positive for COVID-19.  I fear that my employer will not take me back to work even once I test negative.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi :) Is there anything you'd like to talk about? Something on your mind?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm concerned about my job. I have been out of work for the past 5 weeks because I tested positive for COVID-19.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oh I am so sorry to hear that! Are you at least getting sick pay? If not, are you getting advice about help you might be able to access?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oh I am so sorry to hear that! Are you at least getting sick pay? If not, are you getting advice about help you might be able to access?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: (sorry for duplication, not sure what happened there!)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It just keeps getting better...  I applied for the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance and was approved.  The next day, I got an email asking me to verify my identity (I am fine with that.  It actually makes good sense.)...

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So you have been getting some assistance?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: So I did as instructed and got the message on the website thanking me for verification.  The following week I got a physical letter saying I was approved and the award amount per week.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have gone online once a week and qualified, as one is supposed to do, and still I have not received a cent.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I see, so you are really financially struggling at the moment? Is there anywhere else you could apply for assistance? What about a foodbank?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Calling the customer service line is futile.  The computer just plays a recording that the agents are on other calls and then it disconnects the call.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hear you there - I spent a long time on hold for an official matter the other day. I guess that everyone is really desperate for help and advice right now.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been very fortunate.  People in my church have been bringing me food.  I plan on trying to go to the food bank Monday, if they are open.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope that they can help you. My partner and I have used one before and they were very helpful. I felt a bit ashamed but there was no judgement at all.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I actually got so tired of redialing the Department of Labor and Training that I sent an email to the Lieutenant Governor of the state asking for his assistance in getting the matter resolved.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds like a very positive thing to have done. I really hope that they pay some attention to you. This situation is not your fault!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been to this food bank once before, and they actually made me feel very comfortable and welcomed and gave me an information package on other ways the parent organization may be able to assist me.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes they are run by lovely people. Ours gave us a pamphlet for cheap and easy to make recipes too.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am very lucky in that the organization is only 3 miles from me.  I will be looking into their rent assistance and employment assistance programs as well.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So, at least it sounds like you have a good handle on this and are doing everything you can to help yourself, am I right?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have an advantage because I have a professional background in cooking, so I can take random ingredients and turn them into wonderful and nutritious meals.  I just need to have the ingredients.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds very encouraging! It's amazing what you can make even with cheap food. Noodles , for instance, are very versatile :)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: You are right.  I am definitely not going to sit and pout.  I am just a bit frustrated with the system.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It's a very strange situation and I suspect that some of the authorities just feel overwhelmed and have no idea how to cope.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am concerned that my boss may try to not take me back at my job.  Because this is an "at will" state, he can terminate me without cause.  Although he can not legally fire me for being ill with COVID, he can take me back and simply release me the same day saying that I have become redundant.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That would be incredibly immoral of him. Do you feel that he is likely to do such a  thing?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I would not put it past him.  Sadly.  But I have taken the attitude that if it does occur, there is nothing I can do to change the situation.  I would simply pursue a charge against him for wrongful termination, and seek a new job.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is a very rational way to look at things. I really hope that it does not come to thank though! Thank you for talking and I wish you all the best for the coming months.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I may not win the suit, but I would definitely file one.  In 2000, I had an employer fire me without cause.  I sued and won that time.  Not only did they have to pay me back wages for the 90 days that the investigation took place, which was no minor sum,

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am glad that you'd not roll over and accept ill treatment! Well done :)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: they were found to be guilty, so the judge granted me my wages based on the average of 80 hour weeks I had been working, all my vacation time, plus the overtime I would have received, holiday pay, and then to put a nice bow on that gift, he awarded me 5000 dollars in damages because the old company lied and said I had broken the law.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am afraid I need to leave now but thank you for talking :) (can you press the quit button and take the survey?) Best wishes!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My current employer actually knows this happened, because years ago we discussed it, and I showed him the award letter from the Department of Labor and Training, itemizing the judge's findings and the awards.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for your time.  Have a great holiday.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You too!

metadata.situation: I found out that my boyfriend had been lying to me about his entire life, and so the future that he had said we were building towards was all but impossible. I'm trying to figure out if I should stay with him.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello, what is life like for you at the moment?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Infinitely complicated.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Too many decisions. I don't know what to do.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am sorry to hear that but I am happy to listen and help you if I can

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: what sort of things are you trying to decide?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I don't even know where to start.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm trying to decide if I can build trust with him again.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He lied about everything.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well, let's try to take it one problem at a time so's not to get overwhelmed. What is your biggest problem at the moment?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ah, am I to take it that a relationship has recently ended?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: When we met, before we got involved, he said he was divorced. I ended up finding out that he was still legally married. He assured me that they were just a pen's stroke away from being divorced.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That was in March.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I found out three weeks ago that they're actually still living together.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: ANd, no. We haven't broken up yet.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ah I totally hear you .. the old 'we're getting divorced' line. I've been in that one! You are well out of this.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm debating. I don't know what to do.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I feel like a schmuck.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He has such pretty words.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: From personal experience I think that if they say they're going to get divorced and then drag their feet it is never going to happen.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: And he invests so much time and effort into us.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I agree with you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My mind agrees.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My stupid emotions are clouding things.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well, if you were to give him an ultimatum what do you think he would say?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I did.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: LOL

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: And he's still married?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: And he brought his kids to my house so they could meet my kids. He had a conversation with them about why he and their mother had been living the way they had. (in seperate floors of the house)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That was two weeks ago.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: So, yes, he is.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Too soon to tell.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I can tell that you feel that you are being cheated here. I can't tell you what to do but don't you think you deserve better?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I guess that's what I'm trying to figure out. Should I give him time to prove himself now that he's backed into a corner.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It's not for me to say but I wonder if he's really going to change as he has not already.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's not an easy question to answer. He treats me very well. Always has. And he is frantically trying to accomodate me, now htat I know.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I agree with you. It's one of my fears.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: How do your children feel about this? And his?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: MY children (6 and 9) have been living with him in their lives as a male figure who is growing into a father figure. He and I have been together for fifteen months, and part-time living together for six.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: This isn't a new relationship. That's part of the complication, too.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: His kids actually asked if they could come live with me while he and his (ex?) figured their shit out.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes, I can imagine that it is. It is always really difficult when children are involved. I know you would not want your children to be hurt

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It's a messed up situation that COVID has not improved. He was furloughed in May.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Indeed I don't, you're right.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hear you. Covid has disrupted the whole world so might this year! I can't wait for it to be over.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: But now it seems like it will hurt them if I break up with him.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: But it will hurt them more the longer the situation goes on :(

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I wish I could say that I were confident that 2021 would be better, but...

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Too right.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: And this is all a part of why this is not a simple situation.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well it surely could not be worse :)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have no doubt that he loves me very much.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hahahaha! Seems that way.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He didn't make this lie up for me. That's an interesting thing.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He was living the "divorced dad" lie to A LOT of people.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Anybody and everybody who was far enough away to be lied to.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: She lives in her bedroom. Only comes out to work two nights a week. DOesn't want to have anything to do with her kids (5, 9, 11, 13)

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: (sorry was afk let me catch up)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: And she and my BF have been living that way for three years. Over a year before I even met him.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is it possible she is suffering from depression?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I would all but guarantee it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It just worries me that he might treat you the same way if you were ever in the same position

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Here's the other kicker, though...

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: She knows about me.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: (I know. You're right. I thought that as well)

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: And how does she feel about you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: She doesn't care. She just wants to keep the status quo. She likes the money and security.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: (before he was furloughed, he made very good money.)

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I think it would be better if he  were able to come to a sensible financial solution with her. This situation is damaging for everyone.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I agree!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: EVERYBODY!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope I have been able to have been of some help to you :) A very happy New Year to you!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Happy New Year!

dialog.content: You just need to press quit and take the survey - it has to be done at your end :)

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.

metadata.situation: I have been procrastinating on my senior thesis, and the pending deadline is making me extremely nervous and on-edge.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello? Anyone there?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi sorry

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm having trouble getting motivated to finish my senior thesis

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ah! I remember my thesis, a lot of work. One thing for certain, I have a lot of pride over my accomplishment, it was well worth it. When is it due?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: In about a month.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I'm sure you will be able to finish it, sometimes we find ourselves in a slump and need some fresh air blown our way.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you have an advisor who is holding you accountable?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, but I've been really bad about keeping her in the loop. I feel bad when I fall behind, and then I'm fearful of getting back in touch with her.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Whenever I have a large project and lose motivation, I set my goals on paper, then break it down into smaller bites. For example, I will make sure I work one hour on certain days, or call a friend, I generate ideas to keep me on track.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes, I sometimes feel guilty and then don't want to face the music, but actually the best thing to do is recognize you are NOT the first person she knows that got behind. So she is surely experienced with people who need some encouragement. She is the BEST person to go to, actually.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That sounds like a good idea regarding putting it down on paper.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It has always helped me. For example, you can break it down into 4 weeks, then each week write your goals -- maybe put call Advisor or go stop by every week, but I would put that first for the first week.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Then as you check off items, you will see you are moving, even if at a snail's pace, you are moving, and that always encourages me. Sometimes I do not realize how much I AM doing, until I see it on paper. Paper doesn't lie, but my emotions sometimes cloud my thinking.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My other problem is that I'm a perfectionist. I tend to over-analyze and get bogged down, especially when doing research.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Another idea is rewards, when you finish one goal, perhaps put a reward for yourself,  a yogurt with sprinkles or something like that

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You sound like me! I had to learn that I need to strive for EXCELLENCE, not perfection. Perfection will drain us. Do the best I can, leave the rest to God.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is why a time line is good. For example, you make a goal that you will work on your reference and citation page for one hour, after that, you are DONE, If you have time at the end, you can revisit it. The hour is my suggestion, you make your own. lol THAT way, you don't get caught going on and on for 6 hours to make it perfect. One hour is reasonable.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That definitely sounds reasonable. Putting micro deadlines in might be what I need to do to keep me focused.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I do this with EVERYTHING in life because I tend to go on and on too focused and lose track of everything. lol For example, I clean each room for 15 minutes a week. If it needs more, I do more, but I set the timer and you would be surprised how well that works, otherwise, I will spend all my time perfecting one room and the rest is a mess.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Also, your Advisor will know tips to help you too. She has advised a lot of people, her objectivity and experience can give get RIGHT to the heart of any problem, quickly too.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My advisor is a tough woman, I'm not going to beat around the bush. She tends to make everything miserable.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Tough advisors are TOUGH. lol But You sound intelligent and you obviously WANT to do this, it is a goal of yours, I'm sure you can take it!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'll try to keep that in mind. It's something I do feel like I need to finish for my own sake.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It is only one more month of your life. If you buckle down, it will be over and done with before you know it. And I assure you, you will look back in pride at your accomplishments!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That sounds like a wonderful feeling. But so far away.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: My Graduation Day was amazing.  This is what life is about, working NOW for rewards later. It's like a garden, you sow, you weed, you wait for rain and weed some more. You keep waiting and weeding, then later harvest come. It takes time to work a little each day, then time passes whether you lay on your bed or whether you are in the garden working. If you lay on your bed, you get nothing, if you work a little every day, in time, you reap rewards.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's a very poetic way of putting it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Not much in life is easy or free, if we keep working little by little, as time passes, you real a lot of rewards, in fact, you will reap rewards of finishing this thesis for YEARS even decades. It is a great goal and a worthy one to keep at.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'll keep that in mind as I move forward. I really appreciate your help.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I commend you for doing the thesis and I also know it can get weary as time passes, but with some goals on paper a visit to the ADVISOR (hee hee) will set you up right for continued success.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You are very welcome. Have a blessed evening!!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thanks, you too!
